newsitem.title: UK: Moldova to launch $80-100 mln Eurobond in May.
newsitem.headline: Moldova to launch $80-100 mln Eurobond in May.

text.p: Moldova plans to launch its first $80-100 million Eurobond issue on international markets next month, with U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch acting as the agent for the government, Finance Minister Valeriu Chitan said on Saturday.

"We started preparations at the start of this year and are working on the issue of Eurobonds for the sum of $80-100 million," he told Reuters at the annual meeting of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).

Chitan said 10-15 percent of the volume with a maturity of at least five years would be placed with investors in the United States. "The roadshow will take place at the start of May in several financial centres of Europe and two or three U.S. financial centres," he said.
Earlier this year, Chitan said the placement would be in April for $70 million. Initial plans were to issue $50 million worth of Eurobonds with a three-year maturity.

At the EBRD conference he said interest in the issue had picked up since the government started working actively with Merrill Lynch and received a Ba2 sovereign ceiling rating in January from Moody's.
"We already have proposals from several other financial institutions, in particular Dresdner Bank," he said, adding that Japanese banks were also interested.

"After completion of the first stage with Merrill Lynch we will diversify this market," he said. "We expect the bonds to yield about 9-10 percent." The cash from the issue is to be used to service existing foreign debts and to repay pension and salary arrears.

Moldova, a former Soviet republic of 4.4 million people sandwiched between Ukraine and Romania, has raised the level of western investment in its domestic securities from 15 percent last year to about 60 percent now.
"We will continue to expand this and thus lower the yields on domestic securities," he said. "Last year yields were halved over the 12-month period."
